title: Floquet Topological Spin-Valley-Layertronics on a Layered Dice Lattice
authors: Jianqi Zhong, Teng-Fei Ying, Jinyu Zou, Benjamin T. Zhou
abstract: The recent discovery of long-sought dice flat band in layered YCl electride has opened up rich possibilities of correlation and topological physics in dice lattice systems [Nature Communications 17, 2213 (2026), arXiv:2509.05958]. Here, we reveal a plethora of distinctive correlated topological phases in a generic layered dice lattice system at band filling of $ν=4$ under on-site Hubbard interactions: (i) the system is an intrinsic sublattice anti-ferromagnetic (AFM) quantum spin-valley Hall insulator; (ii) a circularly polarized light (CPL) drives the AFM spin-valley insulator into a Floquet odd-parity $f$-wave altermagnet(AM) insulator; (iii) a vertical displacement field turns the Floquet $f$-wave AM insulator into a spin-valley-layer-polarized Chern insulator, with the sign of spin, valley and Chern number all controlled by the direction of the displacement field. Our results not only establish the layered dice lattice as a versatile platform for electrically switchable magnetic and topological phases, but also provide an all-electrical scheme for integrated spin-valley-layertronics for non-volatile information storage and processing.
summary: This work explores topological physics in a layered dice lattice using the Hubbard model. By applying circularly polarized light and external electric fields, the authors demonstrate the ability to switch the system between different correlated topological states, including spin-valley Hall insulators and Chern insulators. This establishes the lattice as a versatile platform for integrated spin-valley-layertronics.
main_problem: The paper aims to reveal and control distinctive correlated topological phases within a layered dice lattice system under on-site Hubbard interactions.
main_result: The system exhibits an intrinsic spin-valley Hall insulator phase, which can be driven into a Floquet f-wave altermagnet and further controlled into a spin-valley-layer-polarized Chern insulator using external fields.
method: The analysis involves using the Hubbard model, calculating low-energy effective Hamiltonians, and determining topological invariants like the Chern number using symmetry analysis.
model_or_system:
The physical platform is a layered dice lattice, modeled using the Hubbard Hamiltonian. The system's behavior is studied at a specific band filling ($
u=4$) and is manipulated by circularly polarized light (CPL) and vertical displacement fields.
key_observables: Spin-valley Chern number ($C_{s,\chi}$), spin-valley-layer locking (SVLL), and the topological phase transitions induced by external fields.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving low-energy effective Hamiltonians and assumes certain symmetry properties (e.g., PT symmetry in the initial state).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dice-lattice geometry, magnetic phase diagrams, the evolution of topological phases under light, and the resulting f-wave altermagnetic band structures with edge states.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the AFM ground state, to analyzing the topological changes induced by CPL (Floquet driving), and finally demonstrating electrical control via a vertical displacement field to achieve spin-valley-layer polarization.
why_interesting: The combination of Floquet engineering (light driving) and electric field gating to control multiple coupled topological orders (spin, valley, layer) in a lattice model is highly relevant for designing artificial quantum materials and quantum simulators.
